question: If $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\2&5\end{bmatrix}$ and $A^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}x\\7\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\1\end{bmatrix}$, determine $x$.
explanation:
Step 1: Use the given matrix relation
The equation is $$A^{-1}\begin{bmatrix}x\\7\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\1\end{bmatrix}$$
Step 2: Premultiply by $A$
Using $AA^{-1}=I$, $$\begin{bmatrix}x\\7\end{bmatrix}=A\begin{bmatrix}3\\1\end{bmatrix}$$
Step 3: Perform the multiplication
Therefore, $$\begin{bmatrix}x\\7\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\2&5\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}3\\1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3+2\\6+5\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}5\\11\end{bmatrix}$$
Step 4: Examine the result
The second component would require $7=11$, which is impossible.
Hence, no value of $x$ satisfies the given matrix equation.

options.D: No value of $x$ satisfies the matrix equation.
